module: Pure functions to decompose a decorated navigation reference of the form `route[?key=value&...][:scope]`. The route part may stay relative ("./options"): this module does not resolve it, it only separates the inline query and the scope and decodes the inline parameters.
usage:
local r = extensions.ui_router_routeReference.parse("menu.options?tab=audio&x=1:scope1")
-- r.route == "menu.options", r.scope == "scope1", r.params == {tab="audio", x="1"}
notes: Inline values stay strings. Explicit parameters passed programmatically win over inline ones on collision (mergeParams, with a warning).
Without '?', the scope separator is the first ':' of the reference; with '?', it is the first ':' after the '?'.
A reference whose route is empty, or whose scope is empty, is treated as an undecorated route (scope nil).

urlDecode.desc: Decodes a query component: '+' becomes a space, then %XX sequences are decoded.

value.desc: Encoded text; a non-string value is returned as is.

parseQuery.desc: Parses an "a=1&b=2" segment into a table. Values stay strings; a repeated key keeps the last value (warning); a bare key ("flag") is an empty string; empty keys are ignored.

parse.desc: Splits "route[?query][:scope]" into its parts. A non-string reference is returned unchanged with empty params.

returns.desc: { route = string, scope = string|nil, params = table<string, string> }

mergeParams.desc: Overlays explicit parameters on inline parameters (copy). Explicit ones win and a warning is logged if the value differs.
